in_arabic.name: طيفور
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من طيف و يدل على الخير و الجمال
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم طيفور مشتق من الجذر اللغوي ط-ي-ف، ويعني الاسم الطيف أو الظل الخفيف، ويدل على الخير والجمال. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم ذكر الطيف في سورة يوسف، حيث قال تعالى: 'فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ بِمُكَيدَاتِهِنَّ أَرْسَلَتْ إِلَيْهِنَّ حُسْنًا فَأَعْجَبْنَ مِنْهُ وَقَطَعْنَ أَيْدِيَهُنَّ وَقُلْنَ حَشَا لِلَّهِ مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَذَا إِلَّا مَلَكٌ مُبَرَّأٌ'، الآية 31، سورة يوسف. ويرتبط الاسم بالمعاني الروحانية والخيرية في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: طيفور
in_urdu.meaning: نام طيفور کا مطلب ہے خوبصورتی اور بھلائی
in_urdu.long_meaning: طيفور نام عربی زبان کے جذر ط-ي-ف سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے طيف يا لائٹ شیڈو. یہ نام حسن اور خوبی کی علامت ہے. اسلامی تقليد میں، یہ نام روحانی اور خلاقانہ معانی کے ساتھ منسلک ہے. جنوبی ایشیائی مسلم معاشرے میں، یہ نام اچھے کردار اور خوبصورتی کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے.

in_hindi.name: तैफुर
in_hindi.meaning: तैफुर नाम का अर्थ है सुंदरता और अच्छाई
in_hindi.long_meaning: तैफुर नाम की उत्पत्ति अरबी भाषा के मूल त-ي-ف से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है तैफ या प्रकाश की छाया। यह नाम सुंदरता और अच्छाई का प्रतीक है। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, यह नाम अच्छे चरित्र और सौंदर्य का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। इस नाम का उपयोग पारंपरिक और आधुनिक दोनों संदर्भों में किया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: طيفور
in_pashto.meaning: د طيفور نوم مطلب د ښه والى او ښکلا دی
in_pashto.long_meaning: طيفور نوم د عربي ژبې د ريښو ط-ي-ف څخه اخيستل شوی دی، چې د طيف يا د رڼا سيوری معنی لري. دا نوم د ښه والى او ښکلا نښه ده. په افغان او پښتني دود کې، دا نوم د روحاني او اخلاقي مفهومونو سره تړلی دی. دا نوم د مثبتو ځانګړتیو او ښايسته اخلاقو د لرونکي شخص لپاره کارول کیږي.

in_english.name: Taifur
in_english.meaning: The name signifies beauty, goodness, and gentle presence
in_english.long_meaning: The name Taifur originates from the Arabic root ط-ي-ف (ṭ-y-f), which means 'specter,' 'apparition,' or 'a light shadow.' In Islamic tradition, this name is associated with spiritual and moral beauty. The Quran mentions 'ṭayf' in Surah Yusuf (12:31), describing a gentle, spiritual presence. The name symbolizes positive attributes such as kindness, beauty, and a gentle soul. Across Muslim cultures, Taifur is used to signify a person with a beautiful character and peaceful demeanor.

data.cultural_impact: The name Taifur holds deep cultural significance in the Islamic world. It is a name that evokes feelings of kindness, compassion, and mercy, all of which are highly valued qualities in Islamic teachings. The use of the name Taifur for children, in particular, is seen as a way to instill these virtues in them from a young age. In Islamic literature and folklore, stories about individuals with this name often highlight their acts of generosity and kindness towards others, serving as an inspiration for those who seek to embody these qualities in their own lives.
data.spiritual_significance: At the core of the spiritual significance of the name Taifur lies the belief in Allah's infinite mercy and compassion towards humanity. The name is a reminder of Allah's love and kindness towards His creation, and the importance of extending that same love and kindness to others in our daily lives. Furthermore, the use of the name Taifur can be seen as a personal invocation of Allah's mercy and compassion, seeking His protection and guidance in times of need. It is a name that carries with it a deep sense of spiritual meaning and significance for those who bear it or are inspired by it.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah The name Taifur carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Taifur is mentioned as the name of the first Umayyad Caliph, Muawiya ibn Abu Sufyan, who ruled from 661 to 680 CE. The name Taifur is derived from the Arabic word 'ta'ifur' which means 'one who is generous and bountiful'. Under his rule, the Umayyad Caliphate expanded and solidified its hold on the Islamic world, effectively ending the Ridda Wars and establishing a period of relative peace and stability.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's Al-Khitat The name Taifur carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Taifur is also mentioned as the name of an early Abbasid military commander, Taifur ibn Ali al-Sulami. He was a prominent figure during the reign of Caliph Harun al-Rashid (763-809 CE) and led several successful military campaigns against the Byzantines and the Umayyads. The name Taifur in this case is likely derived from the Arabic word 'ta'ifur' which means 'lion' or 'tiger', reflecting the commander's fearsome reputation on the battlefield.
